title: Add pcb_bend and pcb_stiffener elements for flex PCBs
description: Add pcb_bend and pcb_stiffener schemas and types to describe bends and bonded reinforcement in flex PCB designs, ensuring flat layout preservation and unit-aware validation.
body:
Flex PCB designs need to describe bends and bonded reinforcement while preserving their flat layout. Add `pcb_bend` and `pcb_stiffener` schemas and types, export them publicly, and register them in `any_circuit_element` and `PcbCircuitElement`.

- Bends carry a board reference, directed `start`/`end` centerline, signed target angle, neutral-surface radius, and moving side.
- Stiffeners carry a board reference, rectangle or resolved polygon geometry, attachment face, material, and separate material/adhesive thicknesses. They do not add copper layers.
- Unit-aware validation rejects degenerate bends, nonfinite/nonpositive dimensions, zero-area polygons, and conflicting shape geometry. Standard generated IDs and optional ownership/name metadata are supported.

Coordinates on these new records are relative to the flat board center. The documentation defines the runtime contract: flat/folded rendering derives CAD positions and orientations without overwriting stored PCB geometry or flat CAD poses. This PR does not implement folding, rendering settings, board material changes, or regional rigid-flex stackups.

Includes examples, coordinate/normalization documentation, and 10 tests covering parsing, validation, public exports, union membership, and JSON round trips. Corresponding TSX props: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/864.

Validation: all 381 tests pass; TypeScript check, ESM/declaration build, Zod lint, snake-case check, changed-file formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. Generated README output was reviewed; unrelated regeneration changes were excluded and the stiffener variants are documented explicitly.

body:
Flex boards currently have no props contract for intended bends or bonded reinforcement. Add exported `PcbBendProps` / `pcbBendProps` and `PcbStiffenerProps` / `pcbStiffenerProps` for `<pcbbend />` and `<pcbstiffener />`.

Bends specify a directed centerline, signed angle, neutral-surface radius, and moving side. Stiffeners support rectangular or polygon geometry, existing PCB placement props, an explicit attachment face/material, and separate material/adhesive thicknesses. Unit-aware parsers reject degenerate centerlines, nonfinite/nonpositive dimensions, degenerate polygon area, and conflicting shape geometry. No important design values are defaulted.

`docs/flex-pcb.md` defines coordinate and normalization semantics and shows two reinforced component sections joined by a flex bridge. It distinguishes bonded stiffeners from integrated rigid-flex stackups and includes a clearly marked future regional-stackup sketch. This PR supplies props only; core JSX registration, Circuit JSON, folding/rendering, board-level DRC, and fabrication exports remain downstream work.

Large imported boards eagerly build a named phase-state map for every renderable. AM62A has 39,779 renderables, and none of those maps are inspected during its normal unobserved render.

Keep ordinary `{ initialized, dirty }` objects in an indexed array. Build the public named map only on first access, using references to those same objects. Render methods directly assign `phaseState.initialized` and `phaseState.dirty`: no packed flags, boolean-array synchronization, state reconstruction, or setter helpers. Once the map is exposed, read it to preserve callers replacing individual entries or the entire map.

Also avoid temporary arrays when checking previous async effects, check the isolated phase before component fields, and skip lifecycle event preparation when no listeners exist. Phase ordering, async barriers, live subscriptions and custom-root/debug behavior are preserved.

Three fresh processes per variant on the frozen AM62A input, in rotating order, with pours disabled:

| Variant | Eval + core render median | Peak RSS median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Merged #4093 baseline | 5.896 s | 1,032 MiB |
| Previous boolean arrays | 4.898 s | 801 MiB |
| Shared state objects | 4.970 s | 884 MiB |

The simpler code retains a **15.7% improvement over baseline** in this batch. It takes **0.072 s (1.5%) longer** and about **83 MiB more peak process memory** than boolean arrays. All nine outputs match: 66,219 records, normalizing only software-version metadata. Timings exclude module startup, serialization, transfer and viewer rendering. The 2-second target remains unmet.

title: Fix net lookup costs across the full render lifecycle
description: Fixes net lookup costs across the full render lifecycle by optimizing the net resolution process, resulting in significant performance improvements during rendering.
body:
## Problem and fix

#4090 accelerated `CreateNetsFromProps`, but its separate existence index did not help later `selectOne("net.NAME", { type: "net" })` calls in vias and traces. The complete render still performed the expensive tree scans. My earlier lookup-only benchmark missed this shift.

Restore `createNetsFromProps` to its original `selectOne` call and move the optimization into shared literal-net resolution. Creation, source traces, vias and pours now resolve through the same scoped index. The index keys off the cached `selectAll("net")` array, so existing ancestor add/remove invalidation rebuilds it. It preserves the first matching net/alias, subcircuit boundaries and misses, respects type constraints before consulting an untyped result cache, and leaves complex/invalid selectors on the existing validation/CSS path.

## Representative benchmark

Replace the lookup-only script with a full `renderUntilSettled()` fixture, also registered in the browser benchmark suite: 1,500 placed parts, 3,000 source traces, 1,500 connected vias, 1,500 pre-routed PCB traces and 1,054 nets. No autorouting or pours. Includes declared and implicitly-created net variants, board-level phase timing, inventories, error detection and full-output SHA-256.

Three fresh sequential processes per declared variant, same dependencies; median local timings:

| Variant | Entire core benchmark | Net creation phase | Source trace phase |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original lookup behavior | 16.13 s | 8.81 s | 0.10 s |
| Released #4090 | 13.96 s | 0.06 s | 7.59 s |
| This replacement | **6.92 s** | 0.07 s | **0.18 s** |

The original-lookup control restores the pre-#4090 call in the otherwise identical release bundle. All nine runs produce **identical hashes and 32,558 records**. The implicit-net sanity comparison also preserves identical output (14.89 s → 12.10 s, one run each).

**Actual AM62A import through eval, pours off:** median local Node evaluation **28.38 s → 12.02 s**, core rendering **25.77 s → 9.97 s**, three fresh processes each. All six outputs preserve the same 66,347 records and hash after excluding only version metadata, with zero pours/errors. Both bundles receive the same existing app compatibility patches; no synthetic cache warming or per-component diagnostic listeners are enabled. These are local measurements, not a production-deployment claim.

Commands, methodology, samples and hashes are committed under `benchmarking/scripts/net-resolution-*`.

## Validation

- `bun run build` and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.
- Relevant selector, base-component, net-name, via, trace-connectivity, shared/exposed-net, copper-pour and group-port tests: **112 passed, 2 existing skips; 5 snapshots unchanged**.
- New cross-phase test fails against released behavior (101 alias scans instead of one), passes with this fix.
- Regression coverage includes typed/untyped reuse, wrong-type requests, duplicate/whitespace aliases, cached misses, ordinary-group ancestor invalidation, nested subcircuit isolation and complex selectors.

title: Avoid repeated CSS tree searches when creating declared nets
description: Reduces the time spent in createNetsFromProps by indexing literal net selectors, significantly improving performance for large imported boards.
body:
Large imported boards spend substantial time in `createNetsFromProps`: each previously unseen `net.NAME` selector walks the component tree through `css-select`, even when all nets are explicitly declared. Profiling the AM62A reference board with pours disabled attributed about 9.2 seconds (41% of sampled CPU time) to this path.

Index literal net selectors from the existing subcircuit-scoped `selectAll("net")` result. A WeakMap keys the index by that cached result array, so the existing ancestor cache invalidation rebuilds it after add/remove operations. Non-literal selectors retain the CSS lookup, and validation and class-alias matching remain intact. No application-specific flags or lifecycle listeners are required.

### Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Relevant base-component, selector, net-name, shared/exposed-net, and group-port tests: **95 passed, 2 existing skips**, including 3 new regression tests.
- `bun benchmarking/scripts/benchmark-net-creation.ts`: **2,524 ms → 11.3 ms** for the cold net-creation lookup step on a tree with 1,500 chips, 15,000 ports, and 1,000 declared nets. Each strategy starts with a fresh tree and verifies that the original net instances are preserved. This is a targeted microbenchmark, not a whole-render speedup.

The regression tests exercise cache reuse, ordinary-group ancestor invalidation, automatic net creation, subcircuit isolation, duplicate names, whitespace class aliases, complex selector fallback, and invalid net names. They assert selector/tree behavior directly because these cache semantics are not visible in a PCB snapshot; existing rendering snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Preserve regional proposals when clearance projection violates the via guard
description: Preserves negotiated routes during regional rerouting when clearance projection would invalidate them due to via guard violations.
body:
Regional rerouting can change a route's point indices while retaining an existing physical via. Clearance projection validates against that intermediate route, so it can move an existing via-to-pad contact and accept the projection. The outer repair guard compares against the pre-reroute geometry, cannot establish the same via correspondence, and rejects the entire regional proposal—including the useful negotiated route.

Pass the pre-reroute routes into clearance projection and use them as its via-guard reference. Both guards now assess the same transition. If projection would invalidate the proposal, its existing rejection path preserves the negotiated routes for outer validation. Whole-board trace and via movement remains available. The outer physical guards, full reference DRC, and incomplete-repair publication policy remain enforced.

- All 15 local tests pass (214 assertions), including the new physical-geometry regression and full-board SRJ18 samples 2, 4, and 13. The new test fails against main.

The candidate shares an eight-rerip budget with the parent search. This lets sample 6 finish its graph while skipping repeated search on boards such as sample 14 that have already spent that budget. Existing greedy orders and budgets remain unchanged. No DRC tolerances, benchmark settings, or timeouts change.

This PR changes only the dependency pin. Implementation and regression test: https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/211 (stacked on #207, which the autorouter already pins).

title: fix: precheck reachability before selective blocker search
description: Adds a reachability check to prevent unnecessary rerouting attempts in the solver when a route is blocked by another route, specifically addressing issues in the routing process for board107-1726.
body:
For board107-1726—the input currently in the PR—the disconnection is created by a rerouting decision:
1. Route 669 occupies a narrow area that route 670 also needs.
2. The solver tries moving 669 to make room for 670.
3. The routes repeatedly interfere with each other, creating a rerouting cycle.
4. To try a different solution, the solver asks: “Can I route 670 without moving 669?”
5. Keeping 669 fixed blocks all seven modeled exits around cmn_1134, isolating the target at cmn_2785.
The original graph has those connections. But the graph of moves allowed for that particular attempt is disconnected. Removing any number of other traces cannot help because 669 blocks the necessary access.
That is why the check belongs in tiny-hypergraph: it tests whether its own proposed constraint—“don’t move 669”—makes the search impossible.
The underlying conflict happens because routing is incremental. A route chosen earlier can occupy access needed by a later route. The solver must then reconsider those choices. The reachability check rejects an impossible alternative; it doesn’t solve the ordering or shared-corridor problem by itself.

**So, for the current board107-1726 test, the main explanation is an impossible constrained rerouting attempt, rather than an incorrectly constructed initial graph. A deeper routing improvement would reconsider the two conflicting routes together or their routing order; the current tiny-hypergraph fix prevents wasting minutes on an alternative that cannot work.**


This PR now targets main directly and excludes #207. It includes the regression test from #210 with the fixed snapshot so the fix is independently mergeable. Validation without #207: all 8 focused blocker-search and reachability tests pass (41 assertions). Full board107 routing has not been rerun on this revised commit.

body:
Stacked on #94.

Adds `UsbSeriesResistorPlacementSolver`, which reports a USB D+/D− series-resistor pair drawn end-to-end on the same row (or column). It recommends nearby placement with clear traces to the corresponding USB ports, without requiring exact coordinate alignment, and reports one `UsbSeriesResistorsNotAligned` issue for the pair. Both resistors and the diagnostic receive matching numbered markers.

The rule follows electrical connectivity from recognized USB pins through one resistor per branch to a shared interface. It skips aligned pairs, different sheets/groups, ambiguous roles or placements, extra resistors, and rail-connected branches. Suggestions are advisory; the solver does not move components or reroute traces.

Both unchanged full-sheet repros emit one new issue. In the placement experiments, arranging the pair in parallel clears it while preserving connectivity. Applying the ESP32's existing R3 flip alone leaves the pair-placement issue, demonstrating the separate coverage.

### RP2040 reference and NEMA23 repro

[Raspberry Pi, Figure 9](https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2040/hardware-design-with-rp2040.pdf#page=12) draws R3/R4 in parallel signal rows. The unchanged [NEMA23 controller](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/nema-23-stepper-controller) places R_USB1/R_USB2 end-to-end.

![Raspberry Pi reference on the left and unchanged tscircuit NEMA23 schematic on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/961ad120-5608-47bc-8a55-6f87e36fb048)

### ESP32-S3 reference and USB ducky repro

[Espressif's USB RC schematic](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-hardware-design-guidelines/en/latest/esp32s3/schematic-checklist.html#fig-usb-rc-schematic) draws the series pair in parallel rows. The unchanged [ESP32 USB ducky](https://tscircuit.com/pixalynx/esp32-usb-ducky) places R3/R4 end-to-end. These comparisons concern schematic readability; the connector and optional capacitor details differ.

![Espressif reference on the left and unchanged tscircuit ESP32 schematic on the right](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/317893ae-4e07-4b23-b6b1-d1c7c675877e)

Validation: 112 tests pass; typecheck, formatting, and browser build pass. Tests cover both real sheets, a TSX before/after with a nearby offset pair and unchanged connectivity, the already-aligned RP2040 controller, topology/scope exclusions, and matching markers.

title: perf: reuse copper alias sets and prune redundant grid checks
description: Reduces the time taken for power trace expansion by reusing resolved copper aliases and eliminating unnecessary grid collision checks, resulting in a performance improvement of 36.1.
body:
Power trace expansion repeatedly resolves the same copper aliases when rebuilding spatial indexes and checks collisions for grid moves that cannot improve the route. On bugreport-107's saved stage input, this change reduces the isolated run from 99.65 s to 63.65 s (36.1%) with identical serialized traces, final solver statistics, and DRC results.

- Reuse resolved alias sets across index rebuilds in a resolver-scoped Map. Compare the complete input snapshot before reuse so in-place alias changes invalidate the entry. Retain only aliases from the currently indexed obstacle collection, clear entries when that collection changes, and resolve transient trace aliases without retaining them.
- Keep the existing per-index alias map, avoiding repeated snapshot validation for rectangles belonging to the same copper object, and reuse the resolved sets for connected pads.
- Apply the existing best-cost rejection before collision checks when a grid move's exact cost is already known. Preserve connector-dependent costs at off-grid octilinear starts.
- Add regressions for alias mutation, resolver isolation, cache lifetime across cloned boards, ordinary/off-grid routing, and live iteration-budget reporting.

Routing budgets, clearance rules, connectivity validation, rollback behavior, and statistics refresh behavior are unchanged.

Validation:

- 83 tests pass across 23 files, with 2,667 assertions; no snapshots updated.
- ESM and declaration builds pass. Full typecheck reports the same 91 existing fixture/test/dependency diagnostics as the unchanged source in this local dependency environment, with no additional diagnostics.
- Differential checks against the unchanged source match on 22 board fixtures and 300 seeded generated grid cases (240 successes, 60 failures), including outputs, termination, iterations, and final statistics. Board phases/statistics also match at 13,049 intermediate checkpoints.
- Bugreport-107: 7,695,924 iterations and 138 relaxed DRC errors in both versions; fresh DRC evaluation returns the identical errors. Output SHA-256: `489f0a92cdf8b59bfe1dcf28d6dbd74b32d296856699ba14ae11b623e09553e6`.
- Benchmark: sequential, unprofiled local runs on the same saved input and dependencies with Bun 1.3.14. This is an isolated-stage, single-board measurement; the full pipeline was not rerun with the patch.

Base: `fix/enforce-connectivity-monotonicity` at `19772f9`, whose tree is identical to the tested autorouter dependency revision `c57511e`. Targeting this branch keeps the PR limited to the optimization and regressions.

Related: #24 and #25 also optimize alias/index handling. This PR retains per-index alias coalescing and shares resolved `ReadonlySet` values across rebuilds; coordinate those overlapping changes before merging.

title: Add shared flex PCB math and reversible CAD poses
description: Introduce a renderer-independent implementation of finite-radius PCB folding and reversible CAD poses, including transformations and geometry handling for PCB components.
body:
Introduce a renderer-independent implementation of finite-radius PCB folding and reversible CAD poses. All shared math uses Circuit JSON's right-handed +Z-up millimeter frame; CAD rotations use intrinsic XYZ degrees.

- Forward/inverse point and direction transforms anchored by the flat PCB mount, so overlapping stacked regions remain invertible.
- Pure, idempotent CAD/Circuit JSON transforms honoring optional `cad_component.is_on_folded_board`. PCB/source records stay untouched; mixed flat/folded inputs normalize independently.
- Surface subdivision at bend tangencies and <=5-degree intervals, preserving flat UVs and face labels.
- Common polygon extrusion and rigid stiffener geometry with adhesive spacing.
- Explicit board ownership and errors for unsupported/ambiguous geometry. Initial scope remains parallel non-overlapping bend chains; rigid mounts and stiffeners must avoid bend zones.

No Three.js, GLTF, browser or native-addon dependency. Consumers provide thin coordinate-frame/mesh adapters.

Validation: nine Bun tests cover analytic quarter turns, signs, oblique axes, arbitrary rotations, inverse round trips, gimbal lock, four-bend stacks, UVs, immutability, idempotence and ambiguous ownership. Typecheck and package build pass. The repository was provisioned through tscircuit/create-repo#75.
